question: Can valid small-sample intervals address the sparse-treatment failure without claiming that software creates missing support?
design: Independent extension of the original offer construction; equal stratum shares and known target weights; n=500; e(0)=0.5 and e(1)=0.02; 3000 replications each of two noise laws
methods: Pooled-variance Student t with n-4 degrees of freedom; requires common normal variance
Bonferroni sum of four exact cell Student t intervals; permits cell-specific normal variances
common_eligibility: All four cells must have at least two observations; unavailable cases retained for every method
targets: Confidence-supported universal-offer decision at illustrative cost 40 USD
metrics: Monte Carlo standard error of each proportion
theory: Conditional on cell counts, normal independent cell observations give exact cell t intervals. Assign alpha/4 to each two-sided interval, sum endpoint errors with absolute contrast weights one half, and use a union bound for at least 95 percent simultaneous coverage. Pooled contrast t is exact only under common variance. Positivity and enough observed cells remain necessary.
resource_limit: 6000 independent replications, CPU only, two minutes
limits: Conservative interval is not an efficient universal solution
No exact guarantee for nonnormal outcomes, estimated population shares or dependent customers
Second study is explicitly motivated by the first study's adverse finding
